# 08 — Syntax highlighting: token/color output for the DEFAULT theme

Target binary: `/workspace/executable` — self-identifies as `bat 0.26.1 (610b77c)`
(`/workspace/executable --version` → `bat 0.26.1 (610b77c)`, exit 0).

Everything in this document was obtained by running the binary. Nothing was disassembled.

---

## 0. Reference command lines and probe environment

The ambient environment of the probe box had `NO_COLOR=1` and `TERM=dumb`.
`NO_COLOR` must be removed for color output; `TERM` turned out to be **irrelevant** to
syntax-highlight colors (see §1.4).

Canonical command used for every capture in this document (256-color mode):

```
env -u NO_COLOR /workspace/executable --color=always --style=plain \
    --theme="Monokai Extended" FILE
```

Variants used for cross-checks:

| Purpose | Command |
| --- | --- |
| 256-color, italics enabled | `env -u NO_COLOR /workspace/executable --color=always --style=plain --theme="Monokai Extended" --italic-text=always FILE` |
| 24-bit truecolor (reveals exact theme RGB) | `env -u NO_COLOR COLORTERM=truecolor /workspace/executable --color=always --style=plain --theme="Monokai Extended" --italic-text=always FILE` |
| No color at all | `env -u NO_COLOR /workspace/executable --color=never --style=plain FILE` |

Exit code is `0` for all successful highlight runs.

### 0.1 The default theme IS "Monokai Extended"

Byte-identical output (md5 of stdout for the same file):

```
$ cd /tmp/hl
$ env -u NO_COLOR /workspace/executable --color=always --style=plain t.c | md5sum
714f3dae68cf48ce35599d52528c1906
$ env -u NO_COLOR /workspace/executable --color=always --style=plain --theme="Monokai Extended" t.c | md5sum
714f3dae68cf48ce35599d52528c1906
$ env -u NO_COLOR /workspace/executable --color=always --style=plain --theme=dark t.c | md5sum
714f3dae68cf48ce35599d52528c1906
$ env -u NO_COLOR /workspace/executable --color=always --style=plain --theme=light t.c | md5sum
557fd5dc9b38e2298f3a7eed04ed4d22      # == "Monokai Extended Light"
```

So: **default == `--theme=dark` == `Monokai Extended`**; `--theme=light` == `Monokai Extended Light`.
`BAT_THEME="Monokai Extended"` produces the same bytes as `--theme="Monokai Extended"`.

Caveat when validating: for *small* inputs, `Monokai Extended`, `Monokai Extended Bright`
and `Monokai Extended Origin` can produce identical bytes (they only differ on some scopes).
They do differ on richer inputs:

```
sample.md  : Monokai Extended        b8bd5505278d8cacb4e2037396e571ac
             Monokai Extended Bright eb60580d82b63c822efdef7f459e3052
             Monokai Extended Origin 5d1fcd8aca6d14b446f48b69702bf683
```

Unknown theme name → warning on **stderr**, default theme used, exit code **0**:

```
$ env -u NO_COLOR /workspace/executable --color=always --style=plain --theme="Nope" t.c
```
stderr, byte-exact (`cat -v`):
```
^[[33m[bat warning]^[[0m: Unknown theme 'Nope', using default.
```
i.e. `ESC [ 3 3 m [bat warning] ESC [ 0 m : ` + `Unknown theme 'Nope', using default.` + `\n`.

---

## 1. Output framing model (the most important section)

### 1.1 One SGR-wrapped run per highlight region

The highlighter produces a sequence of *(style, text)* regions per line. bat writes each
region as:

```
ESC '[' <params> 'm'  <region text>  ESC '[' '0' 'm'
```

where `<params>` is (in this order) the optional attribute codes then the foreground color:

```
[ "1;" if bold ] [ "3;" if italic and --italic-text=always ] [ "4;" if underline ] "38;5;<N>"
```

Observed parameter strings: `38;5;N`, `1;38;5;N`, `3;38;5;N`, `4;38;5;N`, `3;4;38;5;N`.
(Bold and italic were never seen combined — nested markdown `***both***` yields the inner
italic rule *replacing* the bold, see §5.10.)

**bat does NOT coalesce adjacent regions that happen to have the same style.** Every region
gets its own `ESC[...m ... ESC[0m` pair. Example — `int main(void) { return 0; }` in a `.c`
file, byte-exact:

```
$ printf 'int main(void) { return 0; }\n' > t.c
$ env -u NO_COLOR /workspace/executable --color=always --style=plain --theme="Monokai Extended" t.c | cat -v
^[[38;5;81mint^[[0m^[[38;5;231m ^[[0m^[[38;5;149mmain^[[0m^[[38;5;231m(^[[0m^[[38;5;81mvoid^[[0m^[[38;5;231m)^[[0m^[[38;5;231m ^[[0m^[[38;5;231m{^[[0m^[[38;5;231m ^[[0m^[[38;5;203mreturn^[[0m^[[38;5;231m ^[[0m^[[38;5;141m0^[[0m^[[38;5;231m;^[[0m^[[38;5;231m ^[[0m^[[38;5;231m}^[[0m
```

Note `^[[38;5;231m)^[[0m^[[38;5;231m ^[[0m^[[38;5;231m{^[[0m` — three consecutive runs all with
color 231, each individually wrapped. A reimplementation that merges runs will not be
byte-compatible.

### 1.2 Whitespace

* **Yes, whitespace between tokens gets its own escape sequence** whenever it forms its own
  region (which is the common case). Usually it takes the *default text* color (231).
* Whitespace is **not** always default-colored: it takes the color of whatever scope the
  syntax assigned it. Concrete surprises:
  * C/C++ preprocessor: the space after `#include` / `#define` is **141**, not 231
    (`^[[38;5;203m#include^[[0m^[[38;5;141m ^[[0m^[[38;5;186m<^[[0m…`).
  * JavaScript function declarations: every space inside
    `function add(a, b = 2, ...rest)` is **149** (the `entity.name.function` color) — including
    the space between `function` and `add`, and the spaces between parameters.
  * HTML: the space before an attribute name is **149**; after a `<script>` block the leading
    indentation of `  </script>` is **149**.
  * XML `<!DOCTYPE ...>`: the inter-token spaces are **252** (a color that appears nowhere else).
  * `log` syntax: after an `ERROR`/`WARN` token the rest-of-line whitespace is `#F8F8F0`
    (still index 231 after quantization).
* Leading indentation is normally its own region with color 231
  (`^[[38;5;231m    ^[[0m`, `^[[38;5;231m\t^[[0m`).
* Tabs are passed through literally by default (`a\tb` → `^[[38;5;231ma\tb^[[0m`). With
  `--tabs=4` they are expanded to spaces *inside* the colored region:
  `^[[38;5;231ma    b^[[0m`.

### 1.3 Line terminators, blank lines, missing final newline

* **The trailing newline is NEVER colored.** It is emitted after the final `ESC[0m` of the line:
  ```
  $ od -c   # tail of t.c output
  5 ; 1 4 1 m 0 033 [ 0 m 033 [ 3 8 ; 5 ; 2 3 1 m ; 033 [ 0 m ... 033 [ 0 m \n
  ```
* CRLF is preserved verbatim and also uncolored: `...^[[0m\r\n`.
  ```
  $ printf 'int x;\r\nint y;\r\n' > crlf.c   → ... 033 [ 0 m \r \n 033 [ 3 8 ; 5 ; 8 1 m i n t ...
  ```
* **A blank line emits no escape sequences at all** — just the `\n`:
  ```
  $ printf 'a\n\nb\n' > blank.txt
  $ ... | od -c
  033 [ 3 8 ; 5 ; 2 3 1 m a 033 [ 0 m  \n  \n 033 [ 3 8 ; 5 ; 2 3 1 m b 033 [ 0 m \n
  ```
* **A file without a final newline gets no newline added**, and nothing is emitted after the
  last `ESC[0m`:
  ```
  $ printf 'no newline at end' > nonl.txt ; ... | od -c
  033 [ 3 8 ; 5 ; 2 3 1 m n o   n e w l i n e   a t   e n d 033 [ 0 m
  (17 chars of text, stream ends immediately after ESC[0m)
  ```
* There is no leading/trailing "reset" beyond the per-region `ESC[0m`, and no
  `ESC[m`/`ESC[39m` is ever used.

### 1.4 Color depth selection

| Env | Escape form |
| --- | --- |
| default (no `COLORTERM`), any `TERM` incl. `dumb` / `xterm-256color` | 8-bit: `ESC[38;5;<0-255>m` |
| `COLORTERM=truecolor` (also `24bit`) | 24-bit: `ESC[38;2;<r>;<g>;<b>m` |

`TERM=dumb` and `TERM=xterm-256color` give **byte-identical** output. Only `COLORTERM`
switches to truecolor.

Truecolor example:
```
$ env -u NO_COLOR COLORTERM=truecolor /workspace/executable --color=always --style=plain --theme="Monokai Extended" t.c | cat -v
^[[38;2;102;217;239mint^[[0m^[[38;2;248;248;242m ^[[0m^[[38;2;166;226;46mmain^[[0m^[[38;2;248;248;242m(^[[0m^[[38;2;102;217;239mvoid^[[0m^[[38;2;248;248;242m)^[[0m^[[38;2;248;248;242m ^[[0m^[[38;2;248;248;242m{^[[0m^[[38;2;248;248;242m ^[[0m^[[38;2;249;38;114mreturn^[[0m^[[38;2;248;248;242m ^[[0m^[[38;2;190;132;255m0^[[0m^[[38;2;248;248;242m;^[[0m^[[38;2;248;248;242m ^[[0m^[[38;2;248;248;242m}^[[0m
```

### 1.5 No background color in `--style=plain`

`--style=plain` and `--style=numbers` never emit `48;…`. Background appears only for:

* `--highlight-line=N`: every region on that line is prefixed with `48;5;236;`, and the line
  is padded with spaces to the terminal width in a final `^[[48;5;236m<spaces>^[[0m` run:
  ```
  ^[[48;5;236;38;5;81mint^[[0m^[[48;5;236;38;5;231m ^[[0m...^[[48;5;236;38;5;231m}^[[0m^[[48;5;236m<52 spaces>^[[0m
  ```
* Gutter/decorations (`--style=numbers` line numbers are `^[[38;5;246m   1^[[0m ` — foreground
  only; `--style=full` header rules also use 246 and `ESC[1m` for the file name).

### 1.6 Disabling color

`--color=never`, or `NO_COLOR` set with `--color` left at `auto`, produce raw text with zero
escapes. `NO_COLOR=1` combined with an explicit `--color=always` still colorizes (explicit
flag wins). Exit code 0 in all cases.

---

## 2. Palette of the default theme (Monokai Extended)

Every distinct style seen across all 22 languages probed. The 24-bit column is the theme's
true value (obtained with `COLORTERM=truecolor`); the 8-bit column is what the binary emits by
default. **Several distinct theme colors collapse onto the same 8-bit index** — that is
listed explicitly because it makes some categories indistinguishable in default output.
